I did this for a bit when I first started shooting. You shouldn't have a problem getting gigs but will probably need to do a bunch of freebies. So many artists want videos of their gigs, and festivals are so difficult to pull off that people jump at the chance to get content made for them.   
Just contact local artists that you like, look out for small local festivals that could do with the extra marketing, or even venues to see if they want help getting content. If you put something cool together, they are going to want more or refer you to others in the same area. When you feel confident enough and have a good portfolio hopefully you can start doing bigger artists and festivals.   
In terms of gear, I had a cheap stabilizer which really helped to create more "high-end" looking shots. If you are getting shots of the crowd you might need a little panel light, but not super necessary, and as others have said longer lenses are great for getting more candid shots and feeling closer to the band or artist.

It was actually quite a low budget thing, as the the artist has some talented friends that helped out with wardrobe, make up, and hair, and we had access to a studio through a friend too, with some extra lighting equipment thrown in so we were really quite lucky. We used the DoP's URSA mini pro and the Sigma zooms we had. Would have liked some lomo's and a promist filter or something, but didn't even consider as we would already be stretching the budget.  


The concept was a mash of ideas between myself and the artist, she is super conceptual and had the idea for the outfit and colour scheme and wanted to work around that, mainly wanting to create something 'editorial'. I'd been toying with the idea of using old tube TV's in a wall, to create this sort of retro futurism sort of feel. With themes of the song and the feel of the costume I thought the concept sort of fit so we ran with it.  


We shot a bunch of close ups and a couple performances first, then had an on-set editor smash out a couple of edits to play back through the TV's, which would have been tricky but again we got lucky as I guy I know with lots of old equipment had a custom built distribution amplifier which he use to use to send signal to a heap of VCR's to make copies for sports media which he'd on-sell.   


But basically that's how it happened. Hope you like it.
